title: Logic bug: logic equal sqls return different results

comments.text:
Description:
Results of two logic-equal sql queries on Mysql are different, which means a logic bug.

select stu_info.email,stu_score.Excel from stu_info,stu_score where stu_score.id = stu_info.id and stu_info.gender = "f" and stu_info.id < 10;
Empty set (0.00 sec)

select stu_score.Excel ,(select stu_info.email from stu_info where stu_score.id = stu_info.id and stu_info.gender = "f" and stu_info.id < 10) as sub from  stu_score ;
+-------+------+
| Excel | sub  |
+-------+------+
|    87 | NULL |
|    90 | NULL |
|    90 | NULL |
|    88 | NULL |
|    92 | NULL |
|    88 | NULL |
|    79 | NULL |
|    91 | NULL |
|    82 | NULL |
|    85 | NULL |
+-------+------+
10 rows in set (0.00 sec)

How to repeat:

Please do not submit the same bug more than once. An existing bug report already describes this very problem. Even if you feel that your issue is somewhat different, the resolution is likely
to be the same. Because of this, we hope you add your comments to the original bug instead.

Thank you for your interest in MySQL.
